decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch27 row: Kerala topknot, grey streak at the temple, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold ear stud, bare-chested in a plain borderless white mundu, with no chain, sacred thread or forehead marks. His left forearm hangs with no brand showing. His shoulder cloth is draped over the left shoulder rather than knotted at the waist, as on his sheet. The third bearer's face is hidden behind the bier and only his grey beard shows, so he reads as an elder. The priest matches the V13 face, with ash bands, a red dot, the sacred thread and a gold-bordered angavastram, but his lips are closed rather than visibly moving. The shroud covers the body completely. The courtyard has the ring of floor stones, the jackfruit tree, the wood pyre, the walking stick leaning alone and brass open-wick lamps, so it fits panels 1.1 and 1.5. There is no text, noose, gore or anachronism, and the hands are sound. The long caption can sit in the clear pale sky at top centre and left (about x 0.28 to 0.75, y 0.0 to 0.17), clear of every face.

Minor only: Varma's knot sits high and behind his left ear rather than directly above it, and his hair falls in loose curls instead of the sleek dressed hair on his sheet. His pearl ear drops are also missing. The same hair appears in the neighbouring panels 2.2 and 2.5, so the page stays consistent. Otherwise clean: Varma is bare-headed and bare-chested in cream and gold with his necklaces, looking up at Nagoji with an open hand on the unlabelled map. Nagoji has his topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin and gold stud, and wears the white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain, with the forearm scar on his left arm. The map has no writing, the hands are sound, and the war hall matches 2.2. The roof and rafters across the top give room for the balloons.
